# Frozen revision 9 fixed song gain

The oracle executes the unchanged `session_render.render_song` fixed normalization statement and captures the Float32 output before song peak protection. For synthetic inputs it supplies a chosen Float64 meter result and replaces only the post-HP32 input array at that boundary. The original subtraction, exponentiation, and in-place multiplication execute unchanged. Factor metadata evaluates the original statement's parsed right-hand expression in the captured locals; the verifier does not rewrite its equation or derive expected output from native code.

The pinned meter returns a strong NumPy Float64 scalar. Consequently the −20.5 LUFS target subtraction, division, and power remain Double, and the in-place Float32 array multiplication computes each product in Double before a single Float32 store. Rounding the multiplier to Float first is a different operation. This fixed gain is shared by both channels and every song frame, including intro, outgoing transition, and tail. It does not clip, normalize chunks, alter envelopes, or provide peak protection. The existing song protector follows it and retains its separate 160-frame alignment contract.

Ten cases cover the −70 LUFS input boundary, unity, attenuation, high finite loudness, measured quiet/relative-gated/low-frequency/impulse bodies, the original musical body excerpt, and original intro/body/outro/tail probes. Short exact vectors include signed zero, opposite polarity, small values, Float rounding boundaries, and amplitudes above one. The original one-second body input is reused from `loudness-v9`; it is not independently normalized to −20.5. Both musical cases use the same whole-body measurement from all 621 original events and the full 3,711,911-frame original song. The full body is `[393846,3150769)`. Its post-gain loudness and gate counts are recorded and regenerated separately. Body selection and replay remain future production integration work.

The native gain accepts a measurable finite loudness at least −70 LUFS and requires a positive finite Double factor. An unmeasurable body has no gain: the original negative-infinity measurement would produce an infinite multiplier and nonfinite output. Native rejection of that condition is explicit; no fallback gain is inferred. Input samples must be finite and bounded by ±1,000,000. Extreme-domain rejection, rollback, disjoint buffers, floating-point environment behavior, and allocation checks belong to the native harness; they are not hidden inside a broad audio tolerance.

Limits were declared before native comparison: gain dB absolute error `1e-12`, multiplier relative error `2e-15`, complete PCM maximum error `6e-8` and RMS `1e-8`. All short vectors and original boundary probes additionally require exact Float32 bits, including signed zero. Native scalar JSON has exactly `measured_lufs`, `gain_db`, and `linear_gain`; the input loudness must match exactly. Candidate inventory, lengths, hashes, dimensions, finite values, scalar domains, and every output sample are checked. The musical input is frozen exactly for both implementations. Regenerated original boundary input may vary by at most `2e-7` across pinned platforms; complete source hashes identify the freezing platform and do not assert cross-platform byte identity. The existing full-song native event-duration discrepancy remains a separate limitation; these fixtures isolate fixed gain on identical input.

`freeze-gain.py` refuses replacement without explicit `--replace` and never runs in CI. `verify-gain.py --compare .build/tonal-native/gain --evidence .build/tonal-evidence/gain` emits scalar/PCM comparison evidence and one reference/native pair of one-second FLOAT WAV diagnostics. The pair uses the original whole-song gain and is before peak protection, transport fades, or final mastering. It establishes a numerical unit comparison rather than a listening or device-validation claim. No developer fixture or Python dependency enters the app bundle.
